title: How Anti-Worker Lawmakers Are Trying to Muzzle Voters
author: Roxanne D. Brown
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2025/11/IMG_3937-680x510.jpg)

Photograph by Nathaniel St. Clair

Missouri’s Republican lawmakers did exactly what their corporate patrons
demanded in 2017 and rammed through legislation intended to prevent working
people from banding together to fight for better lives.

This gift to the ultra-wealthy prompted a furious backlash, with members of
the United Steelworkers (USW) and other Missourians turning out in force in
2018 to [pass a citizen-driven
referendum](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BLUCVcdNeb31GjsiQQ0eCOZM-2FZ8YGfNbFN9ZQzUtSrzLrLkHEXexe6wBooVOeDwsiRJ3rHL4y28wWoDFxoJEl-2BOhew6Z-2BcO4gAppOS8Zuo-2FLVYbx_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2BWr3nMPkrRXfpuU4vcT6ga0-2BHM-2BbioDxXUhF2PWAgo8oBOfJzaava9QM-2FjB-2FZDX6nSVZka0bTqkz2dJAQe-2BTe-2FjkvDqQwmuEzYGwUk9LPN4ZZlk6KNGrIPwcFbEdaF9cu-2Bp7YGFiSQM9bLDDyaofJZRcEr4C8O7fyBTfNAsThwespZ7-2BKkUqCEdi592vz49qh2dRFmLptNrfF7DBYBzTHEDWEscNf4UjgJ6MhyBKk57neDPY1qCbh5QWTdICX2zFyQ1n1kd7RZL1EeJmxqd2RWnOM0EsILWP9zyhw8alnrkenv16UFwarwseLV4vsUFNmGYGh-2BjY9NXGZQFtWCx29MbOX6LG0EzdqbLums0ZR2kPaczPh7lQHnbNHct2vzpzrUxWesegrv9IUeKVEviq6vFdczo39Gy6YhH4D3mk1ud84-2BTs-2B0tOIXbrX-2FqNDcDqpjOBbfVDY-2BH5fka0AItnIYvqFJ-2Ft3pBD5nCDXWNq5dehQaUjwLCfptCLPHWlUTdxUlxLv-2B5G8nzjoW4QT3IpZpmzn8Bw7xm1J8rLEqdqyZrYYPVeOArO0PDN1P1l7MeH4UHHJ-2BL2FTa0m0R8rCOakBNMpZUWvHg2-2BR2mgKIIEEXdzmU34zF-2FN9fzWyZAmSLgyjrIz-2BjW6WlSYTpMgxtz2QVOJeD8htgZzX8m2sqWIW0fHWXuauO4PvLRWoetFGUVv3xcmgHBPZxg3UMGMdLNV-2FKB5qUi8nRxYpQeC15gRFCc-3D)

You might have expected the corporate loyalists in the General Assembly to be
humbled by this stinging rebuke. You might even have thought that the errant
legislators would correct course and start doing their jobs the right way
after being dealt such a blow.

[much more difficult for the pesky
voters](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BJOS0f7ZtjUUFIsKXoV-2Bpmg-2FpSu5aGhIisSQpdMV61qHeuG22Exf230-2BQwvh7LNvX47-2B3xY-2F4LEdqki2uQ9F1Mec1ecjjP0Km9hmuh5997GJrmxU5-2F50icWDwMSpFh4zJ6v38Udpnt-2BKIFEVQ4Sl2hc-3D0QZD_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2BWr3nMPkrRXfpuU4vcT6ga0-2BHM-2BbioDxXUhF2PWAgo8oBOfJzaava9QM-2FjB-2FZDX6nSVZka0bTqkz2dJAQe-2BTe-2FjkvDqQwmuEzYGwUk9LPN4ZZlk6KNGrIPwcFbEdaF9cu-2Bp7YGFiSQM9bLDDyaofJZRcEr4C8O7fyBTfNAsThwespZ7-2BKkUqCEdi592vz49qh2dRFmLptNrfF7DBYBzTHEDWEscNf4UjgJ6MhyBKk57neDPY1qCbh5QWTdICX2zFyQ1n1kd7RZL1EeJmxqd2RWnOM0EsILWP9zyhw8alnrkenv16UFwarwseLV4vsUFNmGYGh-2BjY9NXGZQFtWCx29MbOX6LG0EzdqbLums0ZR2kPaczPh7lQHnbNHct2vzpzrUxWesegrv9IUeKVEviq6vFdczo39Gy6YhH4D3mk1ud84-2BTs-2B0tOIXbrX-2FqNDcDqpjOBbfVDY-2BH5fka0AItnIYvqFJ-2Ft3pBD5nCDXWNq5dehQaUjwLCfptCLPHWlUTdxUlxLv-2B5G8nzjoW4QT3IpZpqKaUuU-2FoDggspjh6nMi5Kvl7-2By-2FFLi2BFF89n-2FIixoXcEqd-2FO8-2FfTjcUjCiNQwQ-2FvDmjuM6Gfzg37wHsM4XxmVHD18swtXz8rt0j4WUmRBdy9MvzM-2Fr3AOrvc3fmqGG5rMoOYm8j3hvQcPmw-2B0qLaHS0nF3rQ90IgjlKcisLVLbG-2BmDomnw2bOrfd-2B-2BmpR4xJZyJo9xl2meXNzSbdtWJn8-3D)

could scuttle a proposal favored by everyone else.

Thwarting referendums in this way means usurping the will of the people, but
it’s all just another day at the office for a growing number of anti-worker
lawmakers around the country. Their message to voters: Shut your mouths or
we’ll shut them for you.

It’s important to remember that we have a fundamental right to petition and
redress the government—and that includes gathering enough signatures to put an
issue on the ballot and then throwing the matter in front of the entire
electorate for a yes-or-no decision. The referendum enables us to take the
wheel, especially when our elected representatives fail to do what’s right or
act against our interests.

Speaking of which, Missouri Republicans remain angry about the 2018 rollback
of their falsely named “right-to-work” law, aimed at diluting worker power,
decimating unions, and deepening corporate control.

The USW and other pro-worker organizations gathered hundreds of thousands of
signatures—far more than the number required—to force a referendum challenging
the anti-worker measure. Then we put [boots on the
ground](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BHiCFW3si0ymLrTowl5J0sj5YZk5l5pzR3mlIxwhCnYPWYKBLWaBXHwbEGgUbRhJsw-3D-3Dfe4H_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2BWr3nMPkrRXfpuU4vcT6ga0-2BHM-2BbioDxXUhF2PWAgo8oBOfJzaava9QM-2FjB-2FZDX6nSVZka0bTqkz2dJAQe-2BTe-2FjkvDqQwmuEzYGwUk9LPN4ZZlk6KNGrIPwcFbEdaF9cu-2Bp7YGFiSQM9bLDDyaofJZRcEr4C8O7fyBTfNAsThwespZ7-2BKkUqCEdi592vz49qh2dRFmLptNrfF7DBYBzTHEDWEscNf4UjgJ6MhyBKk57neDPY1qCbh5QWTdICX2zFyQ1n1kd7RZL1EeJmxqd2RWnOM0EsILWP9zyhw8alnrkenv16UFwarwseLV4vsUFNmGYGh-2BjY9NXGZQFtWCx29MbOX6LG0EzdqbLums0ZR2kPaczPh7lQHnbNHct2vzpzrUxWesegrv9IUeKVEviq6vFdczo39Gy6YhH4D3mk1ud84-2BTs-2B0tOIXbrX-2FqNDcDqpjOBbfVDY-2BH5fka0AItnIYvqFJ-2Ft3pBD5nCDXWNq5dehQaUjwLCfptCLPHWlUTdxUlxLv-2B5G8nzjoW4QT3IpZpnzFPZWU5izIWyh8pgOvWTL-2BSgq8DKvdlqVvZsNQOfIXZvkvZl-2BMgZcmeC2jj8-2FN7LcrNy5LP5zWuIFjvJxRpX-2Bl4ilXAuUritOpFt6x6Bx-2BF9bA4BZl7Y2gtkzyt-2F1HQwCfKtBV7SbVtJ-2BnV-2FJ6COY23Jfwez64yUUQhlub2-2BJNZH03cQGDXGoyrtDMgfxst4TyP-2BPvy9PGGj7BcgQ6JAs-3D),
mobilizing our activists in a door-to-door outreach effort that drove voters
to the polls and killed the law before it even took effect.

But the pro-worker advocacy didn’t stop there.

referendums, including a commonsense measure in 2024 providing paid sick leave
that Missouri workers need to care for themselves and sick loved ones.
